irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: Represent a two-part OR condition within an arithmetic operand (SUBTRACT right-hand side), where part (x) is a negative boolean condition (does NOT appear as restricted) and part (y) is a positive boolean condition with a subordinate parenthetical qualifier (is restricted in favor of Facilities AND may also secure other pari passu/junior indebtedness)
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: OR is defined as taking operands that resolve to boolean/comparison results, suitable for control flow (IF/AND/OR at the top level). Here, the OR must be buried inside an arithmetic operand (SUBTRACT), and the result must be a MONEY value (aggregate amount of qualifying cash). No existing primitive allows boolean logic to evaluate and then transform into a MONEY value as a single operand - we would need either (1) a boolean-returning OR that can then SELECT which cash balance to subtract (violating type discipline), or (2) a MONEY-returning primitive that embeds internal OR logic without exposing it as a separate boolean node. The current UNSUPPORTED approach is correct, but a candidate extension could be a CONDITIONAL_SUM or FILTERED_AGGREGATE primitive that combines aggregation logic with embedded conditional selection.
irExtensionCandidates.candidateGeneralizedPrimitive: FILTERED_AGGREGATE (operands[], filterCondition) - sums/aggregates only those operands satisfying a complex boolean filter, returning MONEY. This would allow: FILTERED_AGGREGATE([Cash1, Cash2, ...], OR([NOT(restrictedOnBalanceSheet), restrictedInFavorOfFacilities])). Alternatively, MONEY_IF (condition: boolean, trueValue: MONEY, falseValue: MONEY) at the expression level to parallel IF, or a more general CONDITIONAL_OPERAND that wraps any MONEY computation in a gating boolean.

findings.verifierReasoning: The source text provides a complete, unambiguous mathematical definition: a ratio (division) with a clear numerator (a) and denominator (b). The numerator is: Consolidated Secured Debt minus cash and Cash Equivalents meeting specified criteria (marked (x) and (y)). The denominator (b) branches into two cases: (i) for Financial Maintenance Covenant compliance purposes, use Consolidated Maintenance EBITDA; (ii) for all other purposes, use Consolidated EBITDA. Both operands of the division are fully specified. The proposed IR marks this as UNSUPPORTED and claims 'DIVIDE requires both operands,' but the source text explicitly provides both. This is not a genuinely missing operand—it is a representation failure. The IR should record this as a valid DIVIDE expression with the numerator being a subtraction, and the denominator being a conditional (if/then) selection between two EBITDA measures. The IR's claim that the expression is malformed contradicts the explicit, complete structure in the source text. This materially misrepresents the definition because any downstream user of this IR would not understand that the ratio is calculable and would not know which denominator to use depending on context.

findings.verifierReasoning: The source text explicitly conditions the choice of denominator on context: clause (i) applies 'for purposes of determining compliance with the Financial Maintenance Covenant' (use Consolidated Maintenance EBITDA), while clause (ii) applies 'for all other purposes' (use Consolidated EBITDA).
